questions.question: State the meaning of Autocratic leadership style.
questions.solution_html:
• Theory Y
  • Theory X:
  • Theory X assumes that employees are naturally lazy and dislike work.
  • Assumptions:
  • • Employees avoid responsibility
  • • Workers dislike work
  • • Employees require strict supervision
  • • People prefer security over ambition
  • • Workers are motivated mainly by money
  • • Punishment and control are necessary
  • Characteristics:
  • • Authoritarian style of management
  • • Centralised decision-making
  • • Close supervision
  • • Limited employee participation
  • Theory Y:
  • Theory Y assumes that employees are self-motivated and enjoy work.
  • Assumptions:
  • • Work is natural like play or rest
  • • Employees accept responsibility
  • • Workers are capable of self-direction
  • • Employees seek opportunities for growth
  • • Creativity and innovation exist among workers
  • • Participation improves commitment
  • Characteristics:
  • • Democratic leadership style
  • • Decentralised decision-making
  • • Employee participation encouraged
  • • Focus on self-control and self-motivation

• Conceptual Skills
  • Technical Skills:
  • • Ability to use specialised knowledge, methods, and techniques
  • • Involves proficiency in a specific field
  • • Includes knowledge of tools, procedures, and processes
  • • Essential for performing operational activities efficiently
  • • Examples: accounting, production techniques, computer operations
  • Importance:
  • • Helps in solving technical problems
  • • Ensures efficient task performance
  • • Improves operational efficiency
  • Human Skills:
  • • Ability to work effectively with people
  • • Includes communication, motivation, leadership, and coordination
  • • Helps managers understand employee behaviour
  • • Essential for maintaining good interpersonal relationships
  • Importance:
  • • Promotes teamwork and cooperation
  • • Reduces conflicts
  • • Improves employee morale and motivation
  • • Ensures effective communication
  • Conceptual Skills:
  • • Ability to understand the organisation as a whole
  • • Helps in analysing complex situations
  • • Involves strategic thinking and decision-making
  • • Enables managers to relate organisational activities to objectives
  • Importance:
  • • Helps in long-term planning
  • • Facilitates policy formulation
  • • Assists in solving organisational problems
  • • Promotes innovation and strategic vision
  • Variation of Skills Across Management Levels:
  • Top-Level Management:
  • • Requires high conceptual skills
  • • Human skills are also essential
  • • Technical skills are comparatively less important
  • • Responsible for strategic decisions and policy formulation
  • Middle-Level Management:
  • • Requires balanced technical, human, and conceptual skills
  • • Acts as a link between top and lower management
  • • Coordinates departmental activities
  • Lower-Level Management:
  • • Requires high technical skills
  • • Human skills are important for supervising workers
  • • Conceptual skills are comparatively less required
  • • Focuses on day-to-day operations

questions.question: Define organising and explain the characteristics and importance of organising.
questions.solution_html:
• Define organising and explain the characteristics and importance of organising.
  • Organising:
  • Organising is the process of identifying and grouping activities, assigning duties, delegating
  • authority, and establishing relationships among employees to achieve organisational
  • objectives effectively.
  • Characteristics of Organising:
  • • Division of work into manageable activities
  • • Coordination among different departments and individuals
  • • Establishment of authority and responsibility relationships
  • • Delegation of authority to subordinates
  • • Formation of a clear organisational structure
  • • Achievement-oriented process
  • • Continuous and dynamic process
  • • Facilitates cooperation among employees
  • • Defines reporting relationships
  • • Ensures optimum utilisation of resources
  • Importance of Organising:
  • • Facilitates achievement of organisational objectives
  • • Promotes specialization and efficiency
  • • Avoids duplication of work
  • • Clarifies authority and responsibility
  • • Ensures effective coordination
  • • Helps in optimum use of resources
  • • Improves communication within the organisation
  • • Encourages teamwork and cooperation
  • • Facilitates effective control and supervision
  • • Enables adaptation to changes
  • • Assists in employee development
  • • Enhances productivity and profitability
